title: InternalHashError: 'method_descriptor' object has no attribute 'module'
body:
### Summary

Some functions seem to not be able to be cached (but they are pretty commonly used).

I've checked https://stackoverflow.com/questions/27068154/in-python-what-is-a-method-descriptor but it tells to use another package other than `pickle` (in their case, `dill`) which is beyond my control.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

from datetime import datetime as dt


def date_to_timestamp(date):
    return str(int(dt.timestamp(dt.combine(date, dt.min.time()))))


@st.cache()
def foo(date):
    # this function is identity (it just calls date_to_timestamp 
    # but the result is not used here)
    print(date)
    _ = date_to_timestamp(date)
    return date


st.markdown(foo(dt.now()))
```

The entire error message:

In this specific case, it's very likely you found a Streamlit bug so please file a bug report here.

In the meantime, you can try bypassing this error by registering a custom hash function via the hash_funcs keyword in @st.cache(). For example:

@st.cache(hash_funcs={builtins.method_descriptor: my_hash_func})
def my_func(...):
    ...

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no
